title: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner - Cloud fundamentals

questions.text: Which statement best describes cloud computing as defined by AWS?

choices.text: The on-demand delivery of IT resources over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing
A single physical server that a company owns and operates in its own office
Desktop software that is licensed per device and installed locally
A private fiber network that connects two corporate offices

questions.explanation: AWS defines cloud computing as the on-demand delivery of IT resources - such as compute, storage, and databases - over the internet with pay-as-you-go pricing, instead of buying and maintaining physical data centers and servers.

questions.text: Which of the following are advantages of cloud computing described by AWS? (Select all that apply.)

choices.text: Trade capital expense for variable expense
Benefit from massive economies of scale
Increase the time spent running and maintaining data centers

questions.explanation: AWS lists six advantages of cloud computing, including trading capital expense for variable expense, benefiting from massive economies of scale, and stopping guessing capacity. Cloud computing reduces - not increases - the effort spent running data centers.

questions.text: A company runs some workloads in its own on-premises data center and other workloads on AWS, with connectivity between them. Which cloud computing deployment model is this?
questions.explanation: A hybrid deployment connects cloud-based resources with existing on-premises infrastructure, letting an organization extend and grow its infrastructure into the cloud while keeping some resources on-premises.

questions.text: True or False: An AWS Availability Zone consists of one or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity.
questions.explanation: An Availability Zone (AZ) is one or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity in an AWS Region. Multiple isolated AZs let you build highly available applications.

questions.text: Which of the following is one of the pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework?
questions.explanation: The AWS Well-Architected Framework is built on six pillars: operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability. Operational excellence is one of them.

questions.text: Which AWS service provides scalable object storage for data such as images, backups, and static website files?
questions.explanation: Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) is object storage that stores data as objects within buckets and is designed for high durability and scalability. EC2 is compute, VPC is networking, and IAM is identity.

questions.text: Which AWS service provides resizable virtual servers (compute capacity) in the cloud?
questions.explanation: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) provides secure, resizable compute capacity as virtual servers (instances) in the cloud, letting you scale capacity up or down as needed.

questions.text: Which of the following are AWS managed database services? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service and Amazon DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL database service. Amazon S3 is object storage and Amazon EC2 is compute, not database services.

questions.text: Which AWS service lets you run code without provisioning or managing servers, charging only for the compute time you consume?
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda is a serverless compute service that runs your code in response to events and automatically manages the underlying compute resources, charging only for the compute time you use.

questions.text: True or False: Amazon VPC lets you provision a logically isolated section of the AWS Cloud where you can launch resources in a virtual network that you define.
questions.explanation: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) lets you provision a logically isolated section of the AWS Cloud where you launch AWS resources in a virtual network that you define, with full control over IP ranges, subnets, and routing.

questions.text: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which party is responsible for security 'of' the cloud (the physical infrastructure that runs AWS services)?
questions.explanation: AWS is responsible for security 'of' the cloud - the hardware, software, networking, and facilities that run AWS services. The customer is responsible for security 'in' the cloud, such as their data and access management.

questions.text: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which of the following are the customer's responsibility (security 'in' the cloud)? (Select all that apply.)

choices.text: Identity and access management (configuring IAM users and permissions)
Physical security of the data centers

questions.explanation: Customers are responsible for security 'in' the cloud: their data, identity and access management, and client-side encryption. Physical security of the data centers is AWS's responsibility.

questions.text: Which AWS service is used to securely manage user identities and control their access to AWS resources?
questions.explanation: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) lets you securely control access to AWS resources by managing users, groups, roles, and permissions that specify who is authenticated and authorized to use resources.

questions.text: A company has multiple AWS accounts and wants a single bill plus volume pricing discounts across all of them. Which AWS Organizations feature provides this?
questions.explanation: Consolidated billing in AWS Organizations combines usage from all accounts into a single bill and can lower costs because tiered-usage volume discounts are calculated across the combined usage of all accounts.

questions.text: True or False: The AWS pay-as-you-go pricing model means you pay only for the individual resources you consume, with no large upfront commitments required.
questions.explanation: AWS pay-as-you-go pricing lets you pay only for the resources you consume, without upfront commitments or long-term contracts, so you can adapt to changing business needs and avoid over-provisioning.
